newsitem.title: USA: Clinton's Labor Secretary Reich says he quitting.
newsitem.headline: Clinton's Labor Secretary Reich says he quitting.

text.p: U.S. Labour Secretary Robert Reich wrote in Friday's New York Times that he was quitting "a job I love" to spend more time with his family.
"I have the best job I've ever had and probably ever will," Reich wrote. "I also have the best family I'll ever have, and I can't get enough of them," he said.

Reich, 50, an economics lecturer at Harvard University before he joined the Clinton Administration, joined a growing list of President Bill Clinton's Cabinet members who said they would not stay for the second four years.

He wrote that he had informed Clinton about his decision and did not know what he would do next. "I told the boss I'll be leaving, and explained why. Don't know quite what I'll do next," Reich said in the piece titled "My Family Leave Act."
"He understands. He has the same dilemma, and will for at least the next four years," Reich wrote.

He said trying to balance job and family inevitably ended up shortchanging one or the other. "Don't tell me to improve my time-management skills," he wrote. "Teen-age boys don't need you on schedule. A spouse doesn't share intimacies on command."
He has two sons aged 13 and 15 who live with his wife in the Boston area.
A Labour Department spokesman said a replacement for Reich had not yet been decided.
